subject: Incident Notice: increased latency impacting chat streaming - ACMEAnalytics
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident Notice: increased latency impacting chat streaming - ACMEAnalytics

Hi Alex —

We’re reaching out to let you know we’re investigating increased latency on our chat streaming endpoints (v1/chat/stream and v1/chat/streaming) which started around 08:45 PST. Some requests are observing token response delays of 2–4x the usual.

Impact:
- Customers using streaming for real-time chat may see delayed character-by-character output or longer time-to-first-byte.
- Non-streaming generation (standard responses) is mostly within SLA but may see small spikes.

Immediate mitigations we’ve applied:
- Traffic that hit the highest latency tail has been routed to additional GPU capacity in our us-west cluster.
- We’ve toggled an aggressive prefix cache for long-running sessions to reduce KV fetches.

Suggested short-term workarounds (client-side):
1) If you can tolerate slightly larger response chunks, set stream=false to fall back to non-streaming generation for critical flows.
2) Reduce max_tokens_per_chunk from 256 to 128 and increase response polling interval to 300–500ms.
3) Pin calls to a low-latency model variant: redwood-llama-70b-lowlatency-v1 (we’ve prioritized capacity there).

We’ve opened internal ticket RW-11293 and you’ll see updates at the link below. I’ve attached a short latency snapshot we captured for your traffic (latency-snapshot-20260214.csv).

Next steps: we’re continuing to investigate root cause and will follow up within 3 hours with a technical update. If you want a dedicated bridge we can stand one up — let me know.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your UX.

Best,
Hannah
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency-snapshot-20260214.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:36:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident Notice: increased latency impacting chat streaming - ACMEAnalytics

Hannah — thanks for the heads-up and the snapshot. Engineering is on the thread (I’ve looped Sean). Quick notes from infra:
- Initial telemetry shows a spike in KV load for streaming sessions correlated with long chat histories (sessions > 8k tokens).
- One replica’s kernel selection entered a slower execution path under SIMD fallback; we’ve forced a restart on the affected pool.

Immediate ops actions we’re doing now:
- Move ACME traffic to the low-latency pool (confirmed)
- Lower the default streaming chunk size for sessions older than 10 minutes
- Enable early-bail for stalled streams after 1.5s of inactivity to reduce queue head-of-line blocking

Customer-facing mitigation checklist to send to ACME (I suggest we include these in the next update):
- How to turn off streaming (stream=false)
- Model variant recommendation (redwood-llama-70b-lowlatency-v1)
- Short-term config: max_tokens=1024, chunk_size=128, polling_interval=400ms

I’ll post another update once we have kernel metrics and whether a broader rollback is needed.

—Steph
From: Alex Morgan <alex@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Analytics Support <support@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 11:02:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident Notice: increased latency impacting chat streaming - ACMEAnalytics

Thanks for the quick note, Hannah.

This is impacting our live customer chat where streaming is used to show progressive answers. Several customers have reported sluggish typing/feed. We’re seeing time-to-first-token go from ~120ms to 700–1200ms. Our retention and session abandonment metrics spike when streams stall.

Questions:
1) Do you have an ETA for a full remediation or a date when you expect normal latency?
2) If we switch to stream=false for some flows, will that materially affect token billing or throughput on your side?
3) Would Redwood be willing to credit overage charges for the period where we were impacted? This is in-flight during our renewal discussions.

Happy to jump on a call — we’re available 12:00–15:00 PST today.

—Alex
Head of Product Engineering, ACME Analytics
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:10:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident Notice: increased latency impacting chat streaming - ACMEAnalytics

Alex — thanks for the context and the timeline availability. Quick answers up front:
1) ETA: engineering has restored the majority of traffic to low-latency replicas; we expect tail latency to be within normal operational bounds within 6–8 hours while we finish rolling the kernel fix and confirm stability. We’ll update sooner if that changes.
2) Switching to stream=false: this changes how bytes are delivered (batched response vs incremental) but token billing remains the same for generated tokens; however, it typically reduces per-request overhead and can lower your observed latency.
3) Credits: I’m escalating to finance and your AM; we’ll review usage impact and propose a credit. I’ll include the renewal point in my internal notes for leadership.

Attached are concrete mitigation steps and a short checklist you can apply immediately:
- Option A (minimum friction): set stream=false for non-critical chat turns and keep streaming for proactive hints.
- Option B (stronger): pin to redwood-llama-70b-lowlatency-v1 and set chunk_size=128, max_tokens_per_response=1024, polling_interval=400ms.
- Option C (if you use Dedicated): request routing to Dedicated pool RW-DEDI-ACME for the duration (we can fast-track a temporary burst).

Operational notes for engineers (excerpt):
- Client-side: buffer incoming bytes for 150–300ms, then render in short paragraphs rather than character-by-character if UX allows.
- Server-side: we’ve temporarily disabled the speculative attention path that introduced the slow kernel fallback.

I’ve attached a draft postmortem we’ll share internally (postmortem-draft-20260215.md) and set a 60-minute postmortem call for Monday 2026-02-16 — calendar link below. If you want a separate customer-facing postmortem we’ll draft one post-incident and share it prior to the call.

Calendar (proposed): https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=postmortem-acme-20260216
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-14-chat-latency

Would you like the dedicated bridge for 12:00–13:00 PST today? I can have an engineer on the call.

Thanks — we appreciate the patience and will follow up with a technical postmortem.

Best,
Hannah

Attachment: postmortem-draft-20260215.md (Markdown, 6 KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: ACME chat streaming latency (summary & action items)

Team —

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-02-14T08:45–2026-02-14T15:00 PST (tail latency elevated; partial mitigation in place).
- Root cause (prelim): runtime kernel selection entered a SIMD fallback path under a specific memory alignment case for sessions with extremely long histories; this produced per-token CPU stalls and downstream queueing for streaming sessions.

Customer impact: ACME experienced higher time-to-first-token and degraded progressive rendering in their chat product; they escalated due to customer-facing regressions during renewal discussions.

Actions completed:
- Moved ACME traffic to low-latency pool; restarted affected replicas.
- Disabled speculative attention path until kernel fix is validated.
- Published customer mitigation guidance and scheduled customer postmortem.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Engineering (Sean): finish kernel patch and validate across model variants (ETA: 2026-02-18).
- Product (Monica): update model catalog to flag low-latency variants and publish recommended defaults for streaming (ETA: 2026-02-20).
- CS (Steph/Hannah): confirm credit proposal and share customer-facing postmortem (ETA: 2026-02-17).
- Reliability (Hannah): create an automated alert for SIMD-fallback occurrences and add to runbook (ETA: 2026-02-16).

Follow-ups: I’ll consolidate engineer notes into the postmortem doc (postmortem-draft-20260215.md) and share the customer-facing version after product review. Please update the ticket RW-11293 with progress and link to PRs.

Thanks for the quick coordination.

—Hannah
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
